independent_acceptance_claim_checks.scope: Existing reported Problems F1 and F2 only; bounded independent scientific acceptance, not a repeated whole-paper review.

checks.reason: The literal unrestricted tube-Wolff projection statements fail. The report's unit horizontal segments lie in B(0,1), are essentially distinct on a fixed M-delta position/angle grid, and all containing r-tubes admit O((1+r/(M delta))^2) members, hence a fixed tube-Wolff constant. For f(z)=z their projected full shadings lie in [-1,1] x [-delta,delta], contradicting Proposition 7.1 with epsilon=1/2 at small delta. Every positive subshading has projected area / r-neighborhood area at most 2 delta/r, contradicting Lemma 7.12 at r>delta^(1-epsilon^2). The family fails the stronger convex Wolff condition, so it is not a counterexample to Proposition 6.8 or the main dimension conclusions. The independent cubic witness f=450+3t/2+t^2/200 yields g=1-f/450+tf/135000=t^3/27000000 in M_f, with zero 2-jet at 0, so the cinematic separation asserted on p.44 also fails without normalization. A general rotation does not preserve the fixed twisted projection. The inspected later sticky v2 has v_n>=1/2 and normalized Lemma 7.3 with f(0)=0; it is comparison evidence only, not verified historical version equivalence. The core supporting proof is affected; repairability does not reduce Major.

Definition 1.3 allows arbitrarily small positive measure error chosen after the geometric eta. With epsilon=(3-alpha)/4, the true gap d=3-epsilon-alpha=3epsilon, not (3-epsilon)/2. The published choice kappa=(3-epsilon)eta/6 does not force the displayed contradiction; at alpha=5/2 and epsilon=1/8 its exponent margin is negative. The support-centered packing inequality gives (r/rho)^d <= C(r rho)^(-kappa), and scale bounds yield delta^(-eta d)<=C delta^(-2kappa). Choosing kappa=eta d/4 yields the required contradiction. Report handles moving packing centers to support, fixed-factor thinning, enlarging the containing ball and taking delta small after fixed measure/line-density constants. This is a valid conditional repair of the deduction from Theorem 1.5, not a certification of that theorem's whole proof. Error is in a main theorem derivation and remains Major despite local repair.
